issue.title: Serve the machine-capacity display report from the artifact index instead of a 17 s filesystem walk

task_type_fields.proposal: Serve the machine-capacity display report from the persistent artifact index instead of a filesystem artifact walk. Today `machine_capacity_report()` (src/sase/core/runner_slots/_machine_capacity.py) rebuilds `runner_slots.scan.json` through `collect_runner_slot_records` whenever the admission token changes. The research for epic sase-1q5 measured that walk at about 17 s and 0.45 GB of transient heap. Phase sase-1q5.7 rate-limited display rescans from 30 s to 120 s and memoized the parsed scan cache, so the walk now runs at most once per 120 s in a TUI worker thread. Its transient heap still feeds young-generation GC pauses in the long-lived TUI. An index-backed capacity query (active, non-terminal records only, through sase-core per the Rust core boundary) would make the display feed cost O(active rows). Measure first with the post-restart remeasure recipe in docs/contribute/perf-runbook.md, and confirm with tools/tui_freeze_report that capacity walks still appear before building it.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Epic sase-1q5's plan scoped this out explicitly ("An index-backed capacity query is out of scope. If the walk still shows up, record a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP"). Phase sase-1q5.7 recorded it as note #1. It needs a new sase-core query surface and admission-parity tests, which the epic's bounded phases did not cover.

issue.creation_reason: Epic sase-1q5 rate-limited but did not remove the capacity feed's O(archive) walk; phase sase-1q5.7 proposed an index-backed query as the out-of-scope next step.
